title: External plugins using dnstap must move to the new API

detection.reason: affects plugins you compile into your own CoreDNS build; a custom build is not visible from cluster objects

quote: If you're using `dnstap` in your plugin, you'll need to upgrade to the new API
remediation: Only custom CoreDNS builds with external plugins are affected — rebuild them against the 1.8 dnstap API. Stock images need nothing.

title: External plugins must import github.com/coredns/caddy

detection.reason: affects plugins you compile into your own CoreDNS build; a custom build is not visible from cluster objects

quote: *all* plugins need to fix the import path from: `github.com/caddyserver/caddy` to `github.com/coredns/caddy`
remediation: Only custom builds are affected: change the caddy import path and rebuild. Stock images need nothing.

title: Outgoing zone transfers move to the transfer plugin — in-block `transfer to` in kubernetes stops parsing

detection.reason: read from the option KEY names the agent extracts inside each Corefile plugin block of every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns (agent 0.4.58+; older agents leave this NOT_DETECTABLE) — keys only, never values; import lines are not followed — the kubernetes block; the other converted plugins have sibling rules (secondary is hinted: its still-required `transfer from` projects to the same key)

quote: outgoing zone transfers now use this plugin: *file*, *auto*, *secondary* and *kubernetes* are converted. For this you must change your Corefile
remediation: Rewrite every `transfer to …` line inside file, auto, secondary and kubernetes blocks as a top-level `transfer { to … }` block in the same server block, as the 1.8.0 notes show; the in-block form is rejected by 1.8.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*transfer\\s+to\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed line is an in-block transfer that 1.8 refuses to parse

title: Outgoing zone transfers move to the transfer plugin — in-block `transfer to` in secondary stops parsing

detection.reason: the projection keeps option KEYS only: `transfer from` (still required inside secondary) and the moved `transfer to` both project as `transfer`, so the key cannot settle it

quote: outgoing zone transfers now use this plugin: *file*, *auto*, *secondary* and *kubernetes* are converted. For this you must change your Corefile
remediation: Rewrite every `transfer to …` line inside file, auto, secondary and kubernetes blocks as a top-level `transfer { to … }` block in the same server block, as the 1.8.0 notes show; the in-block form is rejected by 1.8. Inside secondary only `transfer to` moves; `transfer from` stays (and 1.12.2 makes it mandatory).
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*transfer\\s+to\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed line is an in-block transfer that 1.8 refuses to parse

title: A DNS-over-HTTPS server block without a tls config now fails to start

detection.reason: server-block zone lines (https://…) are not collected — only the plugin names inside the block

quote: core: doh support: make no TLS config fatal
remediation: Every `https://` server block needs a `tls` directive from 1.8.0; without one CoreDNS used to start silently and now exits.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*https://")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed DoH server block must carry a tls directive

title: trace: root span names no longer contain the query name/type

detection.reason: tracing backends and their dashboards are outside the cluster inventory

quote: plugin/trace: root span names no longer contain the query data
remediation: Trace searches or dashboards keyed on the span name (which used to embed the query) need to filter on span tags instead.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*trace\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed trace setup emits differently-named root spans after 1.8.0

title: CoreDNS must be granted list/watch on endpointslices (Kubernetes >= 1.19)

detection.reason: the ClusterRole projection keeps only pod-subresource rules, so an endpointslices grant is not visible in the snapshot

quote: CoreDNS must be granted `list` and `watch` access to `endpointslices`.
remediation: Add `endpointslices` (group discovery.k8s.io, verbs list+watch) to the system:coredns ClusterRole before upgrading CoreDNS to 1.8.1+ on Kubernetes 1.19+; without it the kubernetes plugin cannot watch endpoints and new pods stop resolving.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterrole -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name + ": endpointslices list+watch " + (if ([.rules[]? | select((.resources // []) | index("endpointslices")) | .verbs[]?] | (index("list") != null and index("watch") != null)) then "granted" else "NOT granted" end)'  # NOT granted = CoreDNS 1.8.1+ cannot watch EndpointSlices and stops resolving new endpoints

title: forward: max_concurrent overflow now answers REFUSED

detection.reason: read from the option KEY names the agent extracts inside each Corefile plugin block of every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns (agent 0.4.58+; older agents leave this NOT_DETECTABLE) — keys only, never values; import lines are not followed

quote: plugin/forward: respond with REFUSED when max_concurrent is exceeded
remediation: Clients used to see SERVFAIL (which resolvers retry) when `max_concurrent` was hit; from 1.8.1 they see REFUSED, which many resolvers treat as final. Re-check the value against real query rates before the hop.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*max_concurrent\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed limit now turns overflow into REFUSED

title: transfer: outgoing AXFR is served over TCP only

detection.reason: which transport a secondary uses to pull the zone is the secondary's configuration, not this cluster's

quote: plugin/transfer: only allow outgoing axfr over tcp
remediation: Secondaries that pull zones from CoreDNS over UDP stop getting them after 1.8.2; make sure they use TCP for AXFR.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*transfer\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed transfer block serves AXFR over TCP only

title: kubernetes: not-ready endpoints are excluded from EndpointSlice answers

detection.reason: which headless Services have clients that depend on not-ready pods resolving is not knowable from the inventory

quote: plugin/kubernetes: Exclude unready endpoints from endpointslices
remediation: Headless Services whose clients relied on not-ready pods appearing in DNS (StatefulSet bootstrap is the usual case) need `publishNotReadyAddresses: true`, otherwise those pods vanish from answers after 1.8.4.
verifyCommand: kubectl get svc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.clusterIP == "None" and (.spec.publishNotReadyAddresses != true)) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # headless Services printed stop resolving NOT-ready pods after 1.8.4; set publishNotReadyAddresses if clients relied on them

title: metrics: the type label is removed from the request-duration histograms

detection.reason: Prometheus rules and dashboards are not collected

remediation: 1.8.4 drops the `type` (record type) label from `coredns_dns_request_duration_seconds` and `coredns_forward_request_duration_seconds` (coredns/coredns ed3f287fe, label-cardinality fix). Alert rules or dashboards that filter or group those histograms by `type` match nothing afterwards; `coredns_dns_requests_total` keeps its `type` label, so move per-type counting there.
verifyCommand: kubectl get prometheusrules -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec | tostring | test("coredns_(dns|forward)_request_duration_seconds\\{[^}]*type=")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # rules printed filter a request-duration histogram by the type label that 1.8.4 removes

title: coredns_cache_misses_total is deprecated

detection.reason: Prometheus rules and dashboards are not collected

remediation: Rewrite promQL to `coredns_cache_requests_total - coredns_cache_hits_total`; the deprecated series is removed in a later release.
verifyCommand: kubectl get prometheusrules -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec | tostring | test("coredns_cache_misses_total")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # rules printed use the deprecated cache-miss series
coversNotes: plugin/cache: Update cache metrics and add a total cache request counter to follow

title: kubernetes: zone transfers answered only for authoritative zones

detection.reason: which zones a downstream pulls via AXFR is the downstream's configuration

quote: plugin/kubernetes: Only answer transfer requests for authoritative zones
remediation: Secondaries transferring a zone the kubernetes plugin is not authoritative for (a parent or reverse zone it merely serves) get REFUSED after 1.8.5.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*transfer\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed transfer block hands out only authoritative zones after 1.8.5

title: kubernetes: pod names longer than 63 characters are no longer DNS labels

detection.reason: pod names are collected but which clients resolve pods by name is not

quote: plugin/kubernetes: Don't use pod names longer than 63 characters as dns labels
remediation: Pods with names over 63 characters stop resolving as `<pod>.<svc>.<ns>.svc` after 1.8.6 (the label was never RFC-valid). Rename the generating workload if anything resolves them.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^.{64,}")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each pod printed has a name longer than 63 characters and loses its pod DNS label after 1.8.6

title: kubernetes: wildcard queries are deprecated (removed in 1.9.0)

detection.reason: whether any client issues wildcard queries (`*.ns.svc`, `any.ns.svc`) is request-time behaviour

quote: This release will also log deprecation warnings when wildcard queries are received by kubernetes. The wildcard functionality will be completely removed from kubernetes plugin in future releases.
remediation: Find clients that resolve `*.<ns>.svc` / `any.<ns>.svc` style names (1.8.7 logs a warning per query) and move them to explicit names before 1.9.0 removes the feature.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/coredns --tail=5000 2>/dev/null | grep -ci wildcard  # non-zero on CoreDNS 1.8.7+ = clients are still issuing wildcard queries that 1.9.0 stops answering; 0 proves nothing on older versions, which log no warning
